evidence.note: RFC reconnaissance proceeds in a dependency-sensible order (frame headers, blocks, literals, FSE, Huffman, sequences), showing conceptual awareness of subsystem structure but no explicit milestone plan.
The lone TaskCreate lumps all subsystems into a single task ('frame/block parsing, FSE, Huffman, literals, sequences, dictionaries, checksum'); no separate sub-goals or done-conditions per component.
Entire decoder written in one Write call — a monolithic push rather than an ordered walking-skeleton where each layer lands and is verified before the next.

Subsystem-level isolation (Huffman vs RFC example, predefined LL table, repeat-offset logic) appears only reactively during debugging, not as planned milestones — partly belongs to verification facet.

reasoning: The agent showed dependency-aware ordering in its reading and named subsystems in a sensible sequence, but implemented the whole decoder in a single monolithic Write with all components bundled into one task and no per-milestone done-conditions — matching the level-3 anchor ('vague ordering in the agent's head; milestones are just write more code'). It exceeds a pure 0-2 blind monolith because reconnaissance and later debugging did isolate individual subsystems, but it never reaches the level-5 pattern of clear milestones each landed and checkpointed before moving on, since everything was written at once.
